decision: Independent comparison found no required English fidelity or readability revision in the bound current base lesson, including the three recovered visible captions. This is text approval only, not native, display, pixel, retention, accessibility or publication approval.

scope.comparisonBasis: Approved CURRENT modern-us-neutral Chinese lesson, exercises and figure manifest; not an uncorrected historical source snapshot.
reviewed: Current title and printed title; deliberately null chapter/section metadata
All thirteen prose objects: six p objects comprising fourteen flow paragraphs, three empty fig objects and four cap objects
Both written solved-example prompts and complete solutions, including all explanatory qualifications
Conditions, unit words, constants, ordered math tokens, figure references and all three changed visible captions
Current versus pre-recovery/recovered lesson JSON, and local native HTML caption text without browser or image viewing
outOfScope: Re-review of approved Chinese source transcription or scientific amendments
Opening source scans, SVGs, artwork or screenshots; fresh geometry or pixel certification
Native pipeline reruns, browser display, prior mobile failure/recovery, retention, DB or publication
Complete English accessibility or localization of intentionally Chinese source-identity/ARIA labels

method.semanticReview: Read the actual Chinese and English current texts side by side, including all prompt/solution notes and recovered captions. Author statements, native status and prior display recovery did not decide the linguistic outcome.
method.mechanicalSupport: Read-only Node checks independently confirmed ordered dollar-delimited math equality, ordered numeral equality, source_text and source snapshot equality, full errata equality, and figure-manifest entry equality. SHA-256 and byte sizes were recomputed from inspected local files.
method.authorToCurrent: All six p texts equal the original author template after whitespace normalization; the three fig texts remain empty and Light is unchanged. Only cap objects 3, 9 and 10 have changed display text. Current exercises and figures are byte-identical to the author's respective templates.
method.recoveryDiff: Before/after structural comparison found exactly six leaf changes: prose[3,9,10].text becomes Figure 229/230/231 and each changes array gains translation. The recovered lesson is structurally and byte-identical to the current lesson.
method.receiptBindings: All three approved Chinese input bindings and all three current English content bindings match the prepared/native receipts; prepared, author and both native HTML bindings also match.
method.unitBindingConvention: sourceBinding/currentBinding resolve into bindings below; pointers address the actual JSON file. Flow indices are zero-based final p-paragraph indices, excluding fig and cap objects.

units.fidelity: Thermistors and Photoresistors faithfully names both source component types; the printed title retains 113. Both optional chapter and section remain null, with no invented headings.
units.identity: Card IDs, number 113, source pages 276/267, figure IDs 229-232 and exercise count 2 are retained.

units.fidelity: Retains marked resistance-temperature dependence and specifically the semiconductor thermistors discussed here: resistance falls when temperature rises and vice versa. Preserves changing electron/hole carrier numbers, Figure 229 ammeter observation, fixed supply voltage, calibration before temperature inference and distinction between sensing component and complete instrument.
units.readability: Thermistor, ammeter, calibration and readout are clear; the text does not generalize the stated temperature direction to every thermistor.

units.fidelity: Empty fig-229 text, source reference p0276#8, printed page and source-identity label are unchanged.
units.readability: No new English prose is concealed or missing in this figure carrier.
units.limitation: Figure appearance is reused, not viewed.

units.fidelity: Retains radiation absorption followed by heating, temperature-dependent resistance and changed circuit reading. Bolometer is named alongside the source's resistance radiation thermometer. The lit-match/several-kilometers claim remains attributed to historical high-sensitivity instruments, conditional on collection, propagation and background, not a fixed range for every device.
units.readability: The thermal detection mechanism and the limitations of the historical sensitivity example are explicit.

units.fidelity: Current Chinese 图 229 is translated exactly to Figure 229; number and source identity are preserved.

Preserves that light absorption can increase conductivity and decrease resistance, including when material temperature is held constant; possibility wording remains can rather than an unrestricted guarantee.
units.readability: Light-induced conductivity is clearly distinguished from heating.

units.fidelity: Retains fixed supply voltage and semiconductor temperature, baseline Figure 230 and illumination Figure 231, increased current, increased conductivity and decreased resistance. Preserves the distinction between direct illumination-induced change and radiation-mediated heating, and the caveat that real light-sensitive components may still be temperature-dependent.
units.readability: Both controls and both figure roles are unambiguous; no 'never affected by temperature' overclaim.

units.readability: No new English text in this carrier; Figure 230 is named in the neighboring current prose.

units.fidelity: Light was already the approved current caption and remains exactly Light. The source_text and fig-231 source-identity label are unchanged.
units.readability: Clear English illumination label; not falsely counted as a new caption translation.

units.fidelity: Current Chinese 图 230 is translated exactly to Figure 230; number and source identity are preserved.
Current Chinese 图 231 is translated exactly to Figure 231; number and source identity are preserved.

Retains release of previously bound electrons for conduction, holes as missing-electron positions rather than physical cavities, neighboring-electron filling and effective positive-charge motion, both carrier types, and increased carrier count. Preserves the original broad photoelectric-effect name while specifically identifying internal photoconductivity; neither electron escape nor prior bulk heating is required.
units.readability: The hole explanation is concrete and the distinction from external photoemission is clear. All four final paragraphs were checked.

units.fidelity: Retains photoresistor as the component using photoconductivity, illumination-to-resistance-to-current-readout chain, source claims of lightweight/sensitive technological uses, and material/structure/operating-condition limits for a particular component.
units.readability: Clearly distinguishes the resistive component from its readout circuit and avoids universal sensitivity claims.

units.segment: From '1. A hollow conducting sphere' through the copper molar mass.
units.fidelity: Retains hollow conducting sphere in copper sulfate electrolyte; R=5 cm, r=0.5 mm, t=30 minutes, 0.01 coulomb per square centimeter in 1 second, requested mass increase and A=0.0635 kg/mol. Unit translations preserve dimensions and rate interpretation.
units.readability: The radius units, arrival rate and molar mass are explicit; no area/time rate is confused with total accumulated charge.

units.fidelity: Retains r<<R small-hole approximation, absence of a field driving directed ion motion rather than absence of ions, and counting only outer-surface deposition. Preserves S=4 pi R^2=314 cm^2, 30 minutes=1800 seconds, full charge multiplication and 5652 coulombs, Faraday-law formula, copper divalence and previously learned Faraday constant, the already-approved current result m approximately 1.9 times 10^-3 kg, and its interpretation as sphere mass increase.
units.readability: The approximation and each area/time/charge step are spelled out, and the final mass statement is complete.
units.scienceBoundary: Checks faithful transfer of approved current science and corrected arithmetic; does not reopen or independently recertify the existing Chinese scientific correction.

units.segment: From '2. Connect a capacitor' through 'Find the voltage across the resistor.'
units.fidelity: Retains high-voltage supply through R=1 ohm, Figure 232, S=3 times 10^-3 m^2, d=3 times 10^-3 m, Roentgen rays identified as X rays, 10^4 ion pairs per cubic meter in 1 second, charge magnitudes equal to electron-charge magnitude, and complete collection without recombination. The requested voltage is across the resistor, not the capacitor or supply.
units.readability: Correct unit words and clear ion-pair generation rate; the unchanged split math tokens for d and n do not change meaning.

units.fidelity: Retains V=IR, continuous-collection steady state and equal circuit current, opposite ion motion contributing to the same current direction, no double-counting of collection at two plates, and one electron-charge magnitude transferred externally per fully collected pair. Volume Sd times production rate gives pairs collected per second, not accumulated ions. Preserves I=enSd, e=1.6 times 10^-19 coulomb, V=enSdR and the already-approved current final result V=1.4 times 10^-20 volt.
units.readability: The collection/current accounting and generation-rate distinction are fully explained through the final resistor-voltage statement.
units.scienceBoundary: Checks faithful transfer of approved current science and corrected arithmetic; does not reopen or independently recertify the existing Chinese scientific correction.
